title: Hollower
description: Hollower is a mod made for builders. It helps hollowing any build easily and efficiently.
body:
# Hollower

A simple Fabric mod for Minecraft that lets you easily select, highlight, and hollow out large builds.

## Before/After hollow demonstration

![showcase hollow](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/qYjEdw9s/images/848440d07401b8f7b1cbac25fc12203551b06852.png)

## What does Hollower do?

- **Select an area**: Mark two corners to define a box in your world.
- **Cast**: Instantly highlight all visible blocks inside your selection.
- **Hollow**: Remove the inside of your selection, leaving only the outer shell.
- **Undo**: Restore the last hollowed area if you make a mistake.
- **Multi-level undo**: Undo multiple hollow or cast actions, not just the last one.
- **Fast and smooth**: Designed for large builds and big selections.

## Why use Hollower?

- **Save time**: No more breaking blocks one by one.
- **Perfect for builders**: Quickly create hollow structures, clear out interiors.
- **Easy to use**: Simple commands, no technical setup needed.
- **Safe**: Undo mistakes with a single command.
- **Client-side only**: No need to install on servers.

## How to use

`/hollower pos1` — Set the first corner of your selection (where you are standing).

`/hollower pos2` — Set the opposite corner of your selection.

`/hollower cast <depth>` — Highlight all visible blocks in your selection. You can use this multiple times to add more blocks. (Optional: `depth` set how much layer to keep)

`/hollower undocast` — Undo the last cast action. Use this if you want to remove the most recently highlighted blocks.

`/hollower clear` — clear all the casted blocks.

`/hollower unselect` — remove selection and clear all casts.

`/hollower hollow` — Hollow out everything inside your selection, leaving only the outer shell.

`/hollower undo` — Undo the last hollow or restore action. You can use this multiple times to go back further.

## Troubleshooting

- If the mod doesn't show up, make sure it's in your `mods` folder and you're using Fabric.
- For crashes or issues, please include your `latest.log` and any `crash-reports` when reporting a bug.
